71	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory MonObj
72	open scoped CategoryTheory.MonObj
73	
74	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
75	
76	namespace Pic0
77	
78	variable {kbar : Type u} [Field kbar] [IsAlgClosed kbar]
79	
80	variable (C : Over (Spec (.of kbar)))
81	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
82	    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
83	
84	/-- **The Albanese universal property of `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` — Milne Proposition III.6.1,
85	with the symmetric power supplied as data.**
86	
87	Let `C` be a smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve over an algebraically
88	closed field `k̄`, let `A` be an abelian variety over `k̄`, and let `φ : C ⟶ A` be
89	*pointed* at `P₀`. Suppose given
90	
91	* `D : SymPowData C (genus C)` — the `g`-th symmetric power with its symmetrisation
92	  projection `π` and universal property, and the symmetry of `π` itself (`hproj`);
93	* `f : Sym^g C ⟶ Pic⁰` presented as the symmetrisation of a pointed Abel–Jacobi map
94	  `aj` (`hf : π ≫ f = aj(P₁) + ⋯ + aj(P_g)`, `haj0 : aj(P₀) = η_J`);
95	* the descent datum `hdesc` — a unique `ψ` with `Sym^g φ = f ≫ ψ` (Milne's step 2,
96	  reduced by `Albanese/AlbaneseFromData.lean` §2 to a morphism on a dense open of
97	  `Pic⁰`).
98	
99	Then there is a **unique** `ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A` with `φ = aj ≫ ψ`.
100	
101	Every other ingredient of Milne's proof is discharged in the body: commutativity of
102	both group objects and pointed rigidity for `Pic⁰ ⟶ A` (Milne I.1.4 and I.1.2, via
103	`Albanese/AVSelfProduct.lean`), and the connector in both directions
104	(`Albanese/AlbaneseFromData.lean`). See the module header for why this is a statement
105	about the Albanese *argument* rather than a closed result about the Jacobian. -/
106	theorem albanese_universal_property_of_symPowData
107	    (D : SymPowData C (genus C))
108	    (hproj : ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin (genus C)),
109	      permAut C σ ≫ D.proj = D.proj)
110	    (P0 : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of kbar))) ⟶ C) (i₀ : Fin (genus C))
111	    {A : Over (Spec (.of kbar))}
112	    [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom] [Smooth A.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom]
113	    (φ : C ⟶ A) (hφ : P0 ≫ φ = η[A])
114	    (aj : C ⟶ jacobianScheme C) (f : D.carrier ⟶ jacobianScheme C)
115	    (hf : letI := jacobianScheme_grpObj C
116	      letI : IsCommMonObj (jacobianScheme C) := by
117	        haveI := jacobianScheme_isProper C
118	        haveI := jacobianScheme_smooth C
119	        haveI := jacobianScheme_geomIrred C
120	        exact isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth_of_package _
121	      D.proj ≫ f = powSum (genus C) aj)
122	    (haj0 : letI := jacobianScheme_grpObj C; P0 ≫ aj = η[jacobianScheme C])
123	    (hdesc : letI := jacobianScheme_grpObj C
124	      letI : IsCommMonObj A := isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth_of_package A
125	      ∃! ψ : jacobianScheme C ⟶ A, D.symAVMap φ = f ≫ ψ) :
126	    ∃! ψ : jacobianScheme C ⟶ A, φ = aj ≫ ψ := by
127	  letI := jacobianScheme_grpObj C
128	  haveI := jacobianScheme_isProper C
129	  haveI := jacobianScheme_smooth C
130	  haveI := jacobianScheme_geomIrred C
131	  -- Milne I.1.4 for both group objects (`Albanese/AVSelfProduct.lean`).
132	  letI : IsCommMonObj (jacobianScheme C) :=
133	    isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth_of_package _
134	  letI : IsCommMonObj A := isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth_of_package A
135	  -- Milne I.1.2: a pointed morphism `Pic⁰ ⟶ A` is a homomorphism.
136	  exact exists_unique_albanese_factorisation D f P0 i₀ hproj aj hf haj0 φ hφ
137	    (fun ψ hψ => isMonHom_of_pointed ψ hψ) hdesc
138	
139	end Pic0
140	
141	/-! ## The attribution of `sorryAx`, made checkable
142	
143	`Pic0.albanese_universal_property_of_symPowData` reports `sorryAx`, and it would be
144	easy — and wrong — to read that as a gap in the Albanese argument. The theorem below
145	is the *same statement with `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` replaced by an arbitrary abelian variety
146	`J`*, and it is **axiom-clean**:
147	
148	```
149	#print axioms albanese_universal_property_of_symPowData_generic
150	  -- [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]
151	#print axioms Pic0.albanese_universal_property_of_symPowData
152	  -- [propext, sorryAx, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]
153	```
154	
155	The two differ only in the target group object. So the entire `sorryAx` residue of
156	the specialised form is `Pic0.jacobianScheme` — i.e. the Picard representability seam
157	upstream of this leg — and **none** of it is the Albanese argument. This is the
158	measurement that turns "the argument is complete" from a claim in a docstring into
159	something a later session can re-run.
160	
161	It also drops the curve hypotheses: nothing in Milne's III.6.1 argument, once the
162	symmetric power is given, uses that `C` is a curve. The genus enters only as the
163	number `g` of factors. -/
164	
165	/-- **The Albanese universal property with an arbitrary abelian variety as target.**
166	
167	Milne Proposition III.6.1 in its widest honest form: for *any* object `C`, any `g`,
168	any symmetric-power datum `SymPowData C g`, and any two abelian varieties `J`, `A`
169	over `k̄`, a pointed `φ : C ⟶ A` factors uniquely through a pointed `aj : C ⟶ J` whose
170	symmetrisation is `f`, given the descent datum.
171	
172	Axiom-clean. Its role is twofold: it is the reusable statement (nothing about curves
173	or the Jacobian is needed), and comparing its axiom set with that of
174	`Pic0.albanese_universal_property_of_symPowData` attributes the latter's `sorryAx`
175	entirely to the Picard seam. See the section note above. -/
176	theorem albanese_universal_property_of_symPowData_generic
177	    {kbar : Type u} [Field kbar] [IsAlgClosed kbar]
178	    (C : Over (Spec (.of kbar))) (g : ℕ)
179	    (D : SymPowData C g)
180	    (hproj : ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin g), permAut C σ ≫ D.proj = D.proj)
181	    (P0 : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of kbar))) ⟶ C) (i₀ : Fin g)
182	    {J A : Over (Spec (.of kbar))}
183	    [GrpObj J] [IsProper J.hom] [Smooth J.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom]
184	    [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom] [Smooth A.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom]
185	    (φ : C ⟶ A) (hφ : P0 ≫ φ = η[A])
186	    (aj : C ⟶ J) (f : D.carrier ⟶ J)
187	    (hf : letI : IsCommMonObj J := isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth_of_package J
188	      D.proj ≫ f = powSum g aj)
189	    (haj0 : P0 ≫ aj = η[J])
190	    (hdesc : letI : IsCommMonObj A := isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth_of_package A
191	      ∃! ψ : J ⟶ A, D.symAVMap φ = f ≫ ψ) :
192	    ∃! ψ : J ⟶ A, φ = aj ≫ ψ := by
193	  letI : IsCommMonObj J := isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth_of_package J
194	  letI : IsCommMonObj A := isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth_of_package A
195	  exact exists_unique_albanese_factorisation D f P0 i₀ hproj aj hf haj0 φ hφ
196	    (fun ψ hψ => isMonHom_of_pointed ψ hψ) hdesc
197	
198	end AlgebraicGeometry

noncomputable def symPowDataTrivial {K : Type*} [Category K] [CartesianMonoidalCategory K]
    [HasFiniteProducts K] (C : K) (n : ℕ) : SymPowData C n where
  carrier := ∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)
  proj := 𝟙 _
  desc := fun {T} h _ => ⟨h, by simp, fun u hu => by simpa using hu⟩

    MonObj.permAut (K := Type) Bool σ ≫ (symPowDataTrivial (K := Type) Bool 2).proj

  intro hall
  have h2 : MonObj.permAut (K := Type) Bool (Equiv.swap (0 : Fin 2) (1 : Fin 2)) = 𝟙 _ := by

  set p : (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin 2 => Bool)) := Pi.lift
    (fun i => fun _ : PUnit => decide (i = (0 : Fin 2))) PUnit.unit with hp

        = Pi.π (fun _ : Fin 2 => Bool) (0 : Fin 2) p from congrFun e0 p, c0] at c1

10	# The symmetric power as an *interface*, and the two maps it produces
11	
12	Milne's proof of the Albanese universal property (*Abelian Varieties* III.6
13	Proposition 6.1) uses the `n`-th symmetric power `Sym^n C` only through its
14	**universal property**: every `S_n`-symmetric morphism `C^n ⟶ T` factors uniquely
15	through the symmetrisation projection `π : C^n ⟶ Sym^n C`.
16	
17	At this Mathlib pin the *object* `Sym^n C` does not exist — there is no quotient of
18	a scheme by a finite group action (`analogies/m3-route-audit.md` sizes the
19	construction at roughly 2400–3800 lines, and mathlib's `SymmetricPower` is for
20	modules). Writing `Sym^n C := sorry` makes every downstream equation a statement
21	about a junk term, which is why `Albanese/AlbaneseUP.lean` keeps its obligations
22	unproved rather than discharging them against a meaningless definition.
23	
24	This file takes the other route: it **names the interface** as a structure
25	`SymPowData C n`, and then proves, unconditionally, everything Milne's argument
26	derives from it. The missing geometry is isolated in exactly one place — inhabiting
27	`SymPowData` — and nothing downstream is a statement about `sorry`.
28	
29	## What is proved here (no `sorry`, nothing conditional on unproved statements)
30	
31	* `SymPowData.symAVMap` — Milne's `Sym^n φ`. Given `φ : C ⟶ A` into a *commutative*
32	  monoid object, the `n`-fold sum `powSum n φ` is `S_n`-symmetric
33	  (`MonObj.powSum_perm`, already proved), so the interface descends it. This is the
34	  content of `lem:symmetric_product_av_map`, and it is a construction, not a
35	  hypothesis.
36	* `SymPowData.proj_comp_symAVMap` / `SymPowData.symAVMap_unique` — its defining
37	  equation and uniqueness.
38	* `MonObj.basePointShift` — the morphism `Q ↦ (P₀, …, Q, …, P₀)` placing `Q` in a
39	  designated slot `i₀` and the basepoint elsewhere. Milne's `Q ↦ Q + (n−1) P₀`
40	  factors through it.
41	* `MonObj.basePointShift_comp_powSum` — **the computation that makes the backward
42	  direction of the Albanese connector work**: for a *pointed* `φ` (`P₀ ≫ φ = η[A]`),
43

84	the factor-permuting automorphism of `C^n`. -/
85	
86	/-- **The universal property of the `n`-th symmetric power, as data.**
87	
88	A `SymPowData C n` is a `carrier` (morally `Sym^n C`) together with a symmetrisation
89	morphism `proj : C^n ⟶ carrier` through which *every* `S_n`-symmetric morphism out of
90	`C^n` factors uniquely.
91	
92	This is the interface, not the construction: see `symPowDataOne` for the case `n = 1`,
93	and the module header for why the general case is a separate subproject. -/
94	structure SymPowData (C : K) (n : ℕ) where
95	  /-- The underlying object, morally `Sym^n C`. -/
96	  carrier : K
97	  /-- The symmetrisation projection `π : C^n ⟶ Sym^n C`. -/
98	  proj : (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)) ⟶ carrier
99	  /-- **The universal property.** Every `S_n`-symmetric morphism `C^n ⟶ T` factors
100	  uniquely through `proj`. -/
101	  desc : ∀ {T : K} (h : (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)) ⟶ T),
102	    (∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), MonObj.permAut C σ ≫ h = h) →
103	    ∃! u : carrier ⟶ T, proj ≫ u = h
104	
105	namespace SymPowData
106	
107	variable {C : K} {n : ℕ}
108	
109	omit [CartesianMonoidalCategory K] in
110	/-- Uniqueness of a factorisation through `proj`, in the form used at call sites:
111	two morphisms out of the carrier that agree after `proj` are equal.
112	
113	Note that no symmetry hypothesis is needed: if `u₁` and `u₂` both factor `h` then
114	`h` *is* symmetric (being `proj ≫ u₁` with `proj` symmetric would be the argument,
115	but here we get it more cheaply — apply `desc` to `proj ≫ u₁`, whose symmetry follows
116	from that of `proj` composed with anything). We therefore take the symmetry of
117	`proj` itself as the input. -/
118	theorem hom_ext_of_proj (D : SymPowData C n) {T : K} {u₁ u₂ : D.carrier ⟶ T}
119	    (hproj : ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), MonObj.permAut C σ ≫ D.proj = D.proj)
120	    (h : D.proj ≫ u₁ = D.proj ≫ u₂) : u₁ = u₂ := by
121	  obtain ⟨u, -, huniq⟩ := D.desc (D.proj ≫ u₁) (fun σ => by rw [← Category.assoc, hproj])
122	  rw [huniq u₁ rfl, huniq u₂ h.symm]
123	
124	section SymAVMap
125	
126	variable [BraidedCategory K]
127	
128	/-- **Milne's `Sym^n φ`.** For `φ : C ⟶ A` into a commutative monoid object, the
129	`n`-fold sum `(P₁,…,P_n) ↦ φ(P₁) + ⋯ + φ(P_n)` is `S_n`-symmetric
130	(`MonObj.powSum_perm` — Milne's "clearly this is symmetric"), so the interface
131	descends it to `Sym^n C ⟶ A`.
132	
133	This is `lem:symmetric_product_av_map`: a *construction* from the interface, with no
134	further geometric input. -/
135	noncomputable def symAVMap {A : K} [MonObj A] [IsCommMonObj A]
136	    (D : SymPowData C n) (φ : C ⟶ A) : D.carrier ⟶ A :=
137	  (D.desc (MonObj.powSum n φ) (fun σ => MonObj.powSum_perm n φ σ)).choose
138	
139	/-- The defining equation of `Sym^n φ`: it restores the `n`-fold sum along `proj`. -/
140	@[reassoc]
141	theorem proj_comp_symAVMap {A : K} [MonObj A] [IsCommMonObj A]
142	    (D : SymPowData C n) (φ : C ⟶ A) :
143	    D.proj ≫ D.symAVMap φ = MonObj.powSum n φ :=
144	  (D.desc (MonObj.powSum n φ) (fun σ => MonObj.powSum_perm n φ σ)).choose_spec.1
145	
146	/-- `Sym^n φ` is the *unique* morphism restoring the `n`-fold sum along `proj`. -/
147	theorem symAVMap_unique {A : K} [MonObj A] [IsCommMonObj A]
148	    (D : SymPowData C n) (φ : C ⟶ A) (u : D.carrier ⟶ A)
149	    (hu : D.proj ≫ u = MonObj.powSum n φ) : u = D.symAVMap φ :=
150	  (D.desc (MonObj.powSum n φ) (fun σ => MonObj.powSum_perm n φ σ)).choose_spec.2 u hu
151	
152	end SymAVMap
153	
154	end SymPowData
155	
156	/-! ## §2. Milne's `Q ↦ Q + (n − 1) P₀`, and why it collapses the sum
157	
158	The backward direction of the Albanese connector restricts the symmetric-power
159	equation along `Q ↦ (Q, P₀, …, P₀)`. The whole force of that step is the following
160	computation in the hom-monoid: summing `φ` over such a tuple gives
161	`φ(Q) + φ(P₀) + ⋯ + φ(P₀)`, and a *pointed* `φ` kills every term but the first. -/
162	
163	namespace MonObj
164	
165	variable {C : K}
166	
167	/-- **The basepoint shift `Q ↦ (P₀, …, Q, …, P₀)`**, placing `Q` in the designated
168	slot `i₀` and the basepoint `P₀ : 𝟙_ ⟶ C` in every other slot.
169	
170	Composed with the symmetrisation projection this is Milne's
171	`Q ↦ Q + (n − 1) P₀ : C ⟶ Sym^n C`. -/
172	noncomputable def basePointShift (P0 : 𝟙_ K ⟶ C) {n : ℕ} (i₀ : Fin n) :
173	    C ⟶ (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)) :=
174	  Pi.lift (fun i => if i = i₀ then 𝟙 C else toUnit C ≫ P0)
175	
176	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
177	theorem basePointShift_π (P0 : 𝟙_ K ⟶ C) {n : ℕ} (i₀ i : Fin n) :
178	    basePointShift P0 i₀ ≫ Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) i
179	      = if i = i₀ then 𝟙 C else toUnit C ≫ P0 := by
180	  simp only [basePointShift, Pi.lift_π]
181	
182	section Collapse
183	
184	variable [BraidedCategory K]
185	
186	/-- **The collapse computation.** For `φ : C ⟶ A` into a commutative monoid object
187	which is *pointed* at `P₀` (`P₀ ≫ φ = η[A]`), summing `φ` over the tuple
188	`(P₀, …, Q, …, P₀)` returns `φ` itself:
189	
190	`basePointShift P₀ i₀ ≫ powSum n φ = φ`.
191	
192	Every slot other than `i₀` contributes `toUnit ≫ P₀ ≫ φ = toUnit ≫ η[A] = 1`, the
193	identity of the hom-monoid, so the product collapses to the single factor at `i₀`
194	(`Finset.prod_ite_eq`). This is the entire content of Milne's "restrict along
195	`Q ↦ Q + (g − 1) P₀` and use `φ(P₀) = η_A`". -/
196	theorem basePointShift_comp_powSum {A : K} [MonObj A] [IsCommMonObj A]
197	    (P0 : 𝟙_ K ⟶ C) {n : ℕ} (i₀ : Fin n) (φ : C ⟶ A) (hφ : P0 ≫ φ = η[A]) :
198	    basePointShift P0 i₀ ≫ powSum n φ = φ := by
199	  classical
200	  rw [comp_powSum]
201	  have hterm : ∀ i : Fin n,
202	      basePointShift P0 i₀ ≫ Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) i ≫ φ
203	        = if i₀ = i then φ else 1 := by
204	    intro i
205	    rw [← Category.assoc, basePointShift_π]
206	    by_cases h : i = i₀
207	    · subst h; simp
208	    · rw [if_neg h, if_neg (fun hc => h hc.symm), Category.assoc, hφ, ← Hom.one_def]
209	  rw [Finset.prod_congr rfl (fun i _ => hterm i), Finset.prod_ite_eq]
210	  simp
211	
212	end Collapse
213	
214	end MonObj
215	
216	/-! ## §3. The interface is inhabited: `Sym^1 C = C`
217	
218	`SymPowData` would be worthless if nothing could ever fill it. For `n = 1` the
219	symmetric group is trivial, `C^1 ⟶ C` is an isomorphism, and the universal property
220	is immediate. So the Albanese argument assembled over this interface
221	(`Albanese/AlbaneseFromData.lean`) is a genuine theorem, not a vacuous implication. -/
222	
223	/-- **`Sym^1 C = C`.** The unique projection `C^1 ⟶ C` is an isomorphism, so every
224	morphism out of `C^1` — symmetric or not, since `S_1` is trivial — factors uniquely
225	through it.
226	
227	This inhabits `SymPowData C 1`, witnessing that the interface of §1 is satisfiable.
228	For `n ≥ 2` inhabiting it is the missing scheme-quotient construction. -/
229	noncomputable def symPowDataOne (C : K) : SymPowData C 1 where
230	  carrier := C
231	  proj := Pi.π (fun _ : Fin 1 => C) 0
232	  desc := fun {T} h _ => by
233	    -- `Pi.lift (fun _ => 𝟙 C)` is a two-sided inverse of the single projection.
234	    have hsec : Pi.lift (fun _ : Fin 1 => (𝟙 C)) ≫ Pi.π (fun _ : Fin 1 => C) 0 = 𝟙 C := by
235	      rw [Pi.lift_π]
236	    have hret : Pi.π (fun _ : Fin 1 => C) 0 ≫ Pi.lift (fun _ : Fin 1 => (𝟙 C))
237	        = 𝟙 (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin 1 => C)) := by
238	      apply Pi.hom_ext
239	      intro b
240	      have hb : b = 0 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
241	      subst hb
242	      rw [Category.assoc, Pi.lift_π, Category.comp_id, Category.id_comp]
243	    refine ⟨Pi.lift (fun _ : Fin 1 => (𝟙 C)) ≫ h, ?_, ?_⟩
244	    · change Pi.π (fun _ : Fin 1 => C) 0 ≫ Pi.lift (fun _ : Fin 1 => (𝟙 C)) ≫ h = h
245	      rw [← Category.assoc, hret, Category.id_comp]
246	    · intro u hu
247	      rw [← hu, ← Category.assoc, hsec, Category.id_comp]
248	
249	end CategoryTheory

  intro hall
  have h2 : MonObj.permAut (K := Type) Bool (Equiv.swap (0 : Fin 2) (1 : Fin 2)) = 𝟙 _ := by

1	/-

6	import Mathlib
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Albanese.SymPowInterface
8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Albanese.DenseOpenDescent
9	import AlgebraicJacobian.Albanese.AVCommutative
10	
11	/-!
12	# The Albanese universal property, proved over the symmetric-power interface
13	
14	`Albanese/AlbaneseUP.lean` pins Milne's Proposition III.6.1 in the shape the
15	challenge wants, but its six obligations are stated against `Pic0.SymmetricPower`,
16	a `sorry`-bodied definition. An equation between morphisms out of a junk term
17	carries no information, so those obligations cannot be discharged — and should not
18	be, since discharging them would prove nothing.
19	
20	This file does the mathematics instead. It takes the symmetric power as the
21	**interface** `SymPowData` (`Albanese/SymPowInterface.lean`), which is inhabited
22	(`symPowDataOne`), and proves Milne's argument over it with no `sorry` and no
23	appeal to an unproved statement. What the challenge still owes is then exactly one
24	thing — `SymPowData C g` for `g ≥ 2`, the missing scheme quotient — rather than six
25	entangled gaps.
26	
27	## The two directions of the connector, and why each is now real
28	
29	Milne's proof turns the Albanese equation `φ = aj ≫ ψ` into the symmetric-power
30	equation `Sym^g φ = f^{(g)} ≫ ψ`. Both directions are proved here:
31	
32	* **Forward** (`symAVMap_eq_of_albanese_eq`). Assume `φ = aj ≫ ψ` where the
33	  Abel–Jacobi map is realised, as Milne realises it, through the basepoint shift:
34	  `aj = basePointShift P₀ i₀ ≫ proj ≫ f`. Then `Sym^g φ` and `f ≫ ψ` agree after
35	  `proj`, because pushing `ψ` through the `g`-fold sum is
36	  `map_prod (IsMonHom.monoidHom ψ _)` — this is where `ψ` being a *homomorphism*
37	  is used, and it is exactly Milne's step 5. Uniqueness in the interface then
38	  gives the equation on the carrier.
39	* **Backward** (`albanese_eq_of_symAVMap_eq`). Restrict along
40	  `Q ↦ (Q, P₀, …, P₀)` and collapse: `MonObj.basePointShift_comp_powSum`
41	  (proved in `SymPowInterface.lean`) says the `g`-fold sum of a *pointed* `φ` over
42	  that tuple is `φ` itself. No quotient property is needed for this direction at
43	  all — only the interface's defining equation.
44	
45	## Main results
46	
47	* `albaneseFactorisation_iff` — the connecting biconditional
48	  `(φ = aj ≫ ψ) ↔ (Sym^g φ = f ≫ ψ)`, over the interface. This is the honest form
49	  of `Pic0.albanese_eq_iff_symmetricPower_eq`.
50	* `exists_unique_albanese_factorisation` — **the Albanese universal property**:
51	  given the interface, the birational descent datum, and pointed rigidity, there is
52	  a unique `ψ` with `φ = aj ≫ ψ`. Milne Proposition III.6.1.
53	* `exists_unique_descent_of_section` (§2) — the descent datum supplied from its
54	  geometric source: a morphism on a dense open of the Jacobian. This is where
55	  `extend_to_av` (Milne I.3.2, proved and unconditional) does its work, and it is
56	  the form the eventual `Sym^g C` construction would feed.
57	* `hom_ext_of_dense_open` — the agreement principle used for uniqueness.
58	
59	## What remains, precisely
60	
61	Only `SymPowData C g` for the actual curve and `g = genus C`, together with the
62	birationality of `f^{(g)}` (Milne III.5.1(a)) in the form of a section over a dense
63	open. Everything Milne derives *from* those is proved below.
64	
65	## References
66	
67	Milne, *Abelian Varieties*, §III.6 Proposition 6.1, p. 104; §III.5 Theorem 5.1(a),
68	p. 101; §I.3 Theorem 3.2. Blueprint `thm:albanese_universal_property` in
69	`blueprint/src/chapters/Albanese_AlbaneseUP.tex`.
70	-/
71	
72	set_option autoImplicit false
73	
74	universe v u
75	
76	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory MonObj
77	
78	namespace CategoryTheory
79	
80	/-! ## §1. The connector, in a general cartesian monoidal category
81	
82	Both directions of Milne's biconditional are statements about monoid objects and
83	finite products; no geometry enters. We therefore prove them once, abstractly, and
84	instantiate at schemes in §2. -/
85	
86	section Connector
87	
88	variable {K : Type u} [Category.{v} K] [CartesianMonoidalCategory K]
89	  [HasFiniteProducts K] [BraidedCategory K]
90	
91	variable {C J A : K} {g : ℕ}
92	
93	/-! ### The hypotheses on `f^{(g)}`, and why they are the right two
94	
95	Milne's cycle map is *defined* as the symmetrisation of the Abel–Jacobi map:
96	`f^{(g)} ∘ π = aj(P₁) + ⋯ + aj(P_g)`. That single equation (`hf` below) is the only
97	property of `f^{(g)}` the argument uses, and when `f = D.symAVMap aj` it holds by
98	`proj_comp_symAVMap`. The second hypothesis is Milne's basepoint condition
99	`aj(P₀) = η_J`, part of `lem:abel_jacobi_morphism`.
100	
101	Together they *imply* Milne's identification of `aj` with `Q ↦ Q + (g−1) P₀`
102	followed by `f^{(g)}` — see `basePointShift_proj_comp`, which is
103	`basePointShift_comp_powSum` applied to `aj` itself. So that identification is
104	derived here, not assumed. -/
105	
106	/-- **Milne's identification of the Abel–Jacobi map, derived.** If `f^{(g)}` is the
107	symmetrisation of a *pointed* `aj`, then `Q ↦ Q + (g−1) P₀` followed by `f^{(g)}`
108	is `aj`.
109	
110	This is `basePointShift_comp_powSum` applied to `aj`: the `g`-fold sum of `aj` over
111	`(Q, P₀, …, P₀)` collapses to `aj(Q)` because `aj(P₀) = η_J`. -/

import Mathlib

/-!
# The `g`-fold sum `C^g ⟶ A` and its permutation symmetry

Milne's proof of the Albanese universal property (*Abelian Varieties* III.6
Proposition 6.1) opens with "clearly this is symmetric, and so it factors
through `C^{(g)}`", where "this" is

`C^g ⟶ A`,  `(P₁, …, P_g) ↦ φ(P₁) + ⋯ + φ(P_g)`

for `φ : C ⟶ A` a morphism into an abelian variety. This file supplies that
morphism together with the content behind the word "clearly": its invariance
under permuting the `g` factors. It is the input that the universal property of
the symmetric power `Sym^g C` consumes.

## The mechanism: hom-sets into a group object are commutative monoids

The whole file rests on a Mathlib fact that makes the geometry evaporate. In a
cartesian monoidal category, `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Cartesian/Mon.lean`
equips the hom-set `X ⟶ A` of a monoid object `A` with a `Monoid` structure
whose multiplication is *definitionally* `f * h = lift f h ≫ μ[A]`, and upgrades
it to a `CommMonoid` when `A` is a commutative monoid object (`IsCommMonObj`).
`Over (Spec k̄)` is cartesian monoidal and braided, and an abelian variety is a
commutative group object there.

So the `g`-fold sum is a `Finset.prod` of morphisms, its symmetry is
`Equiv.prod_comp`, and no hand-rolled induction over `Fin g` is needed. Stating
it this way is not a shortcut: it is the correct observation that Milne's
"clearly" is exactly the commutativity of `A`'s group law and nothing else.

## Main definitions

* `MonObj.preHom` — precomposition `(X ⟶ A) →* (W ⟶ A)` as a monoid
  homomorphism. Mathlib gives the hom-set its monoid structure but does not
  record that precomposition respects it; this is what lets `map_prod` move a
  precomposition through the products below.
* `MonObj.permAut` — the automorphism of `∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)` permuting the
  factors along `σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)`.
* `MonObj.powSum` — the morphism `∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C) ⟶ A` sending
  `(P₁, …, P_n) ↦ φ(P₁) * ⋯ * φ(P_n)`, i.e. the product over `i : Fin n` of the
  projections composed with `φ`.

## Main results

* `MonObj.powSum_perm` — **`powSum` is `S_n`-symmetric**:
  `permAut C σ ≫ powSum n φ = powSum n φ`. This is Milne's "clearly this is
  symmetric", and the hypothesis the symmetric-power universal property consumes.
* `MonObj.comp_powSum` — `powSum` is natural in the source.

## Instantiating this at an abelian variety

`powSum` requires `[IsCommMonObj A]`, which is *load-bearing*: without it the
hom-set is only a `Monoid`, the `∏` notation cannot be written, and the symmetry
is false. It is **not** obtained by synthesis, but it *is* available as a theorem on
the project's standard abelian-variety package — use

```
letI := isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth_of_package A
```

(`AlgebraicGeometry.isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth_of_package`,
`Albanese/AVSelfProduct.lean`: Milne §I.1 Corollary 1.4, proved from the Rigidity
Lemma, with the three `A ⊗ A` side conditions discharged).

Earlier revisions of this note said the project *could not* supply `IsCommMonObj`,
because `isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth` (`Albanese/AVCommutative.lean`) carries
hypotheses `[GeometricallyIrreducible (A ⊗ A).hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType (A ⊗ A).hom]
[IsReduced (A ⊗ A).left]` that synthesis cannot discharge. That was a statement about
instance **keying**, not about the mathematics: `(A ⊗ A).hom` is reducibly
`pullback.fst A.hom A.hom ≫ A.hom` (`Over.tensorObj_hom`), and one rewrite puts each
goal in a form mathlib's own instances solve. See `Albanese/AVSelfProduct.lean`.

## Scope

This file deliberately stops at the symmetry statement. It does **not** construct
`Sym^n C`: at this Mathlib pin there is no quotient of a scheme by a finite group
action (see `analogies/m3-route-audit.md`, which scopes that construction at
roughly 2400–3800 lines). What is supplied here is the *input* to the symmetric
power's universal property, which is the half of Milne's symmetrisation step that
does not depend on the quotient existing.

The other half now has a home: `Albanese/SymPowInterface.lean` takes that universal
property as **data** (`SymPowData`) and uses `powSum_perm` below to turn Milne's
`Sym^n φ` into a construction. The quotient is still missing as an *object*, but no
statement downstream of it is a statement about a `sorry` any more.

## References

Milne, *Abelian Varieties*, §III.6 Proposition 6.1, p. 104; blueprint
`lem:symmetric_product_av_map` in
`blueprint/src/chapters/Albanese_AlbaneseUP.tex`.
-/

open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory

namespace CategoryTheory.MonObj

variable {K : Type u} [Category.{v} K] [CartesianMonoidalCategory K]

/-! ## §0. Precomposition is a monoid homomorphism on hom-sets

`Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Cartesian/Mon.lean` gives `X ⟶ A` its monoid
structure with `f * h = lift f h ≫ μ[A]` and `1 = toUnit X ≫ η[A]`, but does not
record that *precomposition* respects it. It does, and bundling it as a
`MonoidHom` is what lets `map_prod` move a precomposition through the finite
products below. -/

/-- **Precomposition with `u : W ⟶ X`, as a monoid homomorphism**
`(X ⟶ A) →* (W ⟶ A)`. Multiplicativity is `comp_lift` (a lift precomposed is the
lift of the precompositions); unitality is uniqueness of the map to the unit
object. -/
noncomputable def preHom {A X W : K} [MonObj A] (u : W ⟶ X) : (X ⟶ A) →* (W ⟶ A) where
  toFun f := u ≫ f
  map_one' := by
    change u ≫ (toUnit X ≫ η[A]) = toUnit W ≫ η[A]
    rw [← Category.assoc]
    congr 1
    exact Subsingleton.elim _ _
  map_mul' f h := by
    change u ≫ (lift f h ≫ μ[A]) = lift (u ≫ f) (u ≫ h) ≫ μ[A]
    rw [← Category.assoc, comp_lift]

@[simp]
theorem preHom_apply {A X W : K} [MonObj A] (u : W ⟶ X) (f : X ⟶ A) :
    preHom u f = u ≫ f := rfl

section PermAut

variable [HasFiniteProducts K]

/-- **The factor-permuting automorphism of `C^n`.** For `σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)`,
the morphism `C^n ⟶ C^n` whose `i`-th component is the `σ i`-th projection; on
points, `(P₁, …, P_n) ↦ (P_{σ 1}, …, P_{σ n})`. -/
noncomputable def permAut (C : K) {n : ℕ} (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) :
    (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)) ⟶ (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)) :=
  Pi.lift (fun i => Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) (σ i))

omit [CartesianMonoidalCategory K] in
@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
theorem permAut_π (C : K) {n : ℕ} (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (i : Fin n) :
    permAut C σ ≫ Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) i = Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) (σ i) := by
  simp only [permAut, Pi.lift_π]

end PermAut

section PowSum

variable [HasFiniteProducts K] [BraidedCategory K]

/-- **The `n`-fold sum morphism `C^n ⟶ A`.** For `φ : C ⟶ A` into a commutative
group object, the morphism sending `(P₁, …, P_n) ↦ φ(P₁) * ⋯ * φ(P_n)`, formed as
the product in the commutative monoid `(C^n ⟶ A)` of the projections composed
with `φ`.

In the Albanese application `A` is an abelian variety and the group law is
written additively: this is `(P₁, …, P_g) ↦ φ(P₁) + ⋯ + φ(P_g)`. -/
noncomputable def powSum {C A : K} [MonObj A] [IsCommMonObj A] (n : ℕ) (φ : C ⟶ A) :
    (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)) ⟶ A :=
  ∏ i, (Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) i ≫ φ)

/-- **Milne's "clearly this is symmetric".** The `n`-fold sum is invariant under
permuting the factors of `C^n`. The proof is exactly the commutativity of the
group law of `A`: in the *commutative* monoid `(C^n ⟶ A)` a finite product is
invariant under reindexing (`Equiv.prod_comp`).

This is the hypothesis consumed by the universal property of the symmetric power
`Sym^n C`, which is what licenses the factorisation `C^n ⟶ Sym^n C ⟶ A`. -/
theorem powSum_perm {C A : K} [MonObj A] [IsCommMonObj A] (n : ℕ) (φ : C ⟶ A)
    (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) :
    permAut C σ ≫ powSum n φ = powSum n φ := by
  classical
  calc permAut C σ ≫ powSum n φ
      = ∏ i, (permAut C σ ≫ Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) i ≫ φ) :=
        map_prod (preHom (permAut C σ)) _ Finset.univ
    _ = ∏ i, (Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) (σ i) ≫ φ) :=
        Finset.prod_congr rfl fun i _ => by rw [← Category.assoc, permAut_π]
    _ = ∏ i, (Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) i ≫ φ) :=
        Equiv.prod_comp σ (fun i => Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) i ≫ φ)

/-- `powSum` is natural in the source: precomposition distributes over the sum. -/
theorem comp_powSum {C A W : K} [MonObj A] [IsCommMonObj A] (n : ℕ) (φ : C ⟶ A)
    (u : W ⟶ (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C))) :
    u ≫ powSum n φ = ∏ i, (u ≫ Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) i ≫ φ) := by
  classical
  exact map_prod (preHom u) _ Finset.univ

end PowSum

end CategoryTheory.MonObj
